title: Fasten a post-op shoe on a practice leg: draw the instep strap back through its D-ring, snug, smooth it closed
instruction: Fasten the post-op shoe on the practice leg: draw its instep strap back through the D-ring until the shoe is snug, then lay the strap back over and smooth it down so that it holds. Then let go of the shoe.
context: A post-operative shoe is worn for weeks after foot surgery or a forefoot fracture, over bulky dressings; bending to the foot is hard for the wearer, so a family member or carer often fastens it. Its straps run through D-rings and fold back onto themselves with hook and loop. The instep strap must be drawn back through its D-ring against the springback of the opened, padded upper until the opening closes, folded back round the ring's bar, laid on its own loop patch and smoothed down along its length so that it holds a pull. The leg hangs from a sprung knee and must not be dragged off its mark. The forefoot strap is already fastened at the start. One arm does the strap work; the other may hold the heel (not required or scored).
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases projected onto the table (x away from the robot, y to the robot's left). Leg: a practice lower leg with a right foot (an adult care-manikin leg, knee down, about 3.5 kg; a foam-filled full-size male display-mannequin lower leg weighted to 3.5 kg will do), the foot wrapped in a padded gauze dressing, hung from a two-axis knee pivot 53 cm above the table and 20 cm behind the middle of the sole (the shin slopes back as when seated), on a stand clamped behind the table. Stand: a 25 mm steel post (about 70 cm) in a bench clamp; at its top a two-axis bracket of two pillow-block pairs on 8 mm steel shafts, the sideways shaft (along the shoe) on top and the flexion shaft (across the shoe) hanging below it, the leg's knee end fixed to the flexion shaft. Each shaft carries a stock steel torsion spring with a stop-collar preload, about 5 N m/rad (sideways) and 18 N m/rad (flexion; e.g. a 180 deg torsion spring of about 0.3 N m per degree), and a stock rotary damper of about 3 N m s/rad on the shaft end (e.g. a viscous rotary damper of that rating with a gear or coupling); check each rate with the spring scale on a lever arm. Set the springs' preload so that the sole just rests on the table. The sole rests on the table, toes toward the robot, the middle of the sole at x 24, y 0, the shoe outlined with tape (its mark). Shoe, already on the foot: an open-toe post-operative shoe, men's Large (e.g. a DARCO MedSurg or Medline post-op shoe, size L; outsole about 29 x 11 cm), navy padded canvas upper, rigid rubber rocker sole, two hook-and-loop straps through plastic D-rings; the dressed toes show past the open toe. The forefoot strap is fastened. The instep strap (25 mm wide) is anchored on the inner (right-arm) side, crosses the instep 4 cm toe-ward of the sole's middle, passes through a black plastic D-ring (opening about 29 x 7.5 mm) on the outer (left-arm) wing of the opening, and folds back onto itself: its end carries the hook patch (about 7 cm, ending at the tab) and a rubber pull tab with a raised bead, its first run the loop patch. If the shoe's own strap or D-ring differs a little in size, use it as it is and keep the 35 mm fastened length. The outer wing (5 cm along the shoe) springs open; drawing the strap until the opening is closed takes about 5 N on the tab (measure with the 0-10 N spring scale on the tab, the same scale used for scoring; trim the splay to suit: a strip of 10 mm closed-cell EVA foam, 50 x 15 mm, slipped under the outer wing at its hinge line pushes it further open; trim its thickness until the 40 mm opening and about 5 N closing pull are met). Behind the opening the upper is closed. A padded heel pull tab stands above the collar. Start: the instep strap threaded through its D-ring and opened outward, about 5 cm of tail out beyond the D-ring with the pull tab standing about 2 cm proud of the upper; the outer wing splayed so that the opening's edges are 40 mm apart under the strap.
scoring: Ruler, pen, phone photo and the 0-10 N spring scale, after the robot has let go and stayed at least 3 cm from the shoe for 1 s. At reset, mark the instep strap with a pen line at the D-ring's outer bar. 0.25 when the mark has moved at least 1 cm back through the D-ring (the strap still through it); 0.5 when the shoe is also snug: the opening's two edges 12 mm or less apart, measured beside the strap's toe-side edge; 0.75 when it is also fastened: at least 35 mm of the hook patch lies fastened on the loop patch (measured along the strap from the first to the last fastened point, unfastened gaps between them included; a point counts as fastened when a business card cannot be slid between hook and loop there); 1.0 when it also holds: hook the spring scale on the tab, pull 5 N along the strap, parallel to the upper and away from the D-ring, for 1 s, and the tab moves less than 3 mm against a pen mark on the strap beneath it (do the pull before measuring the fastened length). A strap laid down without being drawn snug scores at most 0.25. 0 if at any time the leg moves more than 5 cm from its tape mark or the strap comes out of its D-ring, or if the robot is still within 3 cm of the shoe at the end.
reset_notes: Open the instep strap: peel its hook patch off, draw the strap back out through its D-ring until about 5 cm of tail stands out beyond the ring with the pull tab upright, and let the outer wing of the upper spring open; check with a ruler that its edge is 40 mm from the inner edge under the strap and with the spring scale that about 5 N on the tab closes it (re-splay if the padding has relaxed). Re-draw the pen line at the D-ring's outer bar. Leave the forefoot strap fastened. Set the sole back on its tape mark, toes toward the robot. The shoe stays on the foot between trials; the straps are sewn on, so replace the shoe if the instep strap's hook patch clogs or no longer holds the 5 N pull.
fidelity: Leg, foot and shoe: rigid stand-in shapes on one articulation, the leg on a sprung, damped two-axis knee pivot; the opening's outer wing a sprung flap with a rigid D-ring. Strap: 34 hinged thin plates, sliding through the D-ring by contact. Hook and loop: a joint per plate pair forms at >= 2 N measured contact, faces opposed; breaks at 2.5 N peel or 17 N shear (typical, ASTM D5170/D5169). Forefoot strap, dressing, padding visual; strap and D-ring sizes assumed. The 5 N pull: a capped drive.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (valid run); scripted demo: 1.0 (487 steps)
